claims.statement: JWT tokens carry sub, type (access|refresh), ver (user version bumped on disable/delete), and runtime iat/exp; access expires in 60 minutes, refresh in 14 days, and decode runs on a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread so argon2 / jose do not block the event loop.
Settings.model_post_init refuses to boot when app_env != "development" and jwt_secret equals the committed dev default, so production cannot sign admin JWTs with a publicly known key.

Auth routes apply Redis-backed rate limits: login 10/60s per IP, forgot-password 5/300s per IP and 3/900s per email, reset-password 10/300s per IP and 10/900s per email, refresh 20/60s per IP, reflecting the cost of argon2 verify on the 2 vCPU droplet.

Two roles (admin, recruiter) live in app/identity/domain/role.py; require_admin accepts only admin, require_recruiter accepts admin and recruiter so admins implicitly pass every recruiter gate, and the access policies are split framework-free across access/domain (policies.py) and access/application (roles.py) for testability.
installation_dependencies gates every non-auth route on installation state, so the first request after a fresh deploy must complete the admin bootstrap before any other route is reachable.

CapabilityRegistry rejects duplicate capability ids and duplicate routes/resources/slots inside one capability, validates dependency closure, and resolve() rejects mismatched PACK_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_VERSION, SUPPORTED_KERNEL_ABI, pack version, and pack_contract_hash so stale callers cannot bind to a moved contract.

The recruitment pack declares conversation, knowledge, candidate_intake, job_advisory, and channel.zalo; the candidate_intake capability carries the source-owned DESCRIPTOR, while the shipped recruitment_v1_contract.json is the canonical non-executable parity artifact (schema_version=1, contract_hash 2a7c602a...).

Adapters are reachable through registry.resolve() but never appear in export_pack_contract(); the parity test asserts the shipped JSON equals the export and contains no "import" / "factory" strings, locking the contract surface.

The frontend canAccess(role, params, availableResources) mirrors the backend as a UX layer only — recruiters see conversations and projects, every other resource is admin-only, and the file's own comment declares real enforcement is the FastAPI backend.
